clue.text: Travelled, say, by river to try out a vehicle

indicators.note: say tells the solver to take the sound of the preceding word rather than its spelling

parts.note: travelled on horseback or by bike is rode
the Test is a river in Hampshire, famous for trout

explanation.surface: Someone who journeyed by river is taking a new car out for a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns RODE into its sound-alike ROAD; the Test is a chalk-stream river in Hampshire, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A road test is a trial drive of a car on public roads.

clue.text: The vicar's just the chap to call again

parts.note: a vicar is addressed as the Rev, and the 's stands for is
the chap who is exactly right is it, as in 'he's it'

explanation.surface: A vicar is the ideal man to make a second pastoral visit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a sentence the pieces say REV IS IT: the vicar is the one.
explanation.definitionFit: To revisit is to pay another visit, which is what calling again means.

clue.text: No harm can come to the final competitor

indicators.note: the letters come out in a different order, as in 'come apart', so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reassurance that the last runner in the race will be safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come' makes ANCHORMAN from the letters of NO HARM CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: In a relay team the anchorman runs the last leg, the closing member of the side.

clue.text: Brainwork, albeit troublesome at first

parts.note: albeit is a conjunction meaning even though

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word troublesome is used

explanation.surface: Mental effort can be awkward when you are getting started.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought is the activity of the mind, so it is work done by the brain.

clue.text: River engulfs hostelry and small wood

indicators.note: engulfs means the river name swallows the word for an inn inside itself

parts.note: the Spey is a river in Scotland
a hostelry is an inn

explanation.surface: A Scottish river floods a pub and the trees beside it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spey is a Scottish salmon river.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinney is a copse or small area of trees.

clue.text: In Kent the output of coal gives comfort

indicators.note: In places the reworked letters inside the abbreviation for the region

parts.note: Kent is in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

indicators.note: the output of means the letters are processed into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Kentish coal mining is said to cheer people up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the output of' turns COAL into OLAC, which 'In' puts inside SE, the South East of England, where the county of Kent lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is consolation in a time of distress.

clue.text: King lends ear, perhaps, to his malicious defamation

definitions.text: King lends ear, perhaps, to his malicious defamation

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch listens to someone whispering poisonous gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges R (Rex, king) with LENDS EAR; the whole clue also describes the answer, the man whose lies the king hears.
explanation.definitionFit: A slanderer spreads damaging falsehoods about people, the kind of tale a credulous ruler might listen to.

clue.text: Pulse is fast, they found, in Paris

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
ils is the French word for they, the form found in Paris

explanation.surface: Someone in Paris discovers their heartbeat is racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat, but it means edible seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentils are pulses, the dried edible seeds of a leguminous plant.

clue.text: Record once distributed around a Continental city

indicators.note: around tells us the rearranged letters sit on either side of the word for a record
distributed means spread about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: A record from years ago was sold around a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' turns ONCE into CONE, and 'around' wraps those letters about LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne is a large city in Germany, on mainland Europe.

clue.text: Hugo has stories about one of these period pieces

indicators.note: about means the pieces together go round the numeral

parts.note: Victor Hugo was the French novelist
ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Victor Hugo's tales concern an antique from a bygone era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets VICTOR followed by ANA around I; ana, a collection of anecdotes, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoriana are objects made in the reign of Queen Victoria, collected as antiques.

clue.text: White flower, or blue?

definitions.meaning: a flower here is a river, something that flows, and the White branch of one great African river is meant
a pale greenish shade of blue named after that river

explanation.definitionFit: The White Nile is one arm of the great African river, and Nile blue is a pale greenish-blue colour.

clue.text: Forthcoming issue may drive one into this union

definitions.text: Forthcoming issue may drive one into this union

parts.words: Forthcoming issue may drive one into this union
parts.note: issue here means offspring: a baby on the way can force a couple into a hasty marriage

explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun wedding is a marriage hurried along because the bride is pregnant.

clue.text: Recipient of two letters indentified as a grass

definitions.meaning: St Paul wrote two New Testament epistles to his follower of this name
a meadow grass grown for hay

explanation.definitionFit: Paul's two epistles went to this disciple, and the same name belongs to a common pasture grass, Phleum pratense.

clue.text: Social worker known for lack of pretension?

definitions.text: Social worker known for lack of pretension?

parts.words: Social worker known for lack of pretension?
parts.note: a social worker is a colony insect, and one modest in nature would be a lowly one

explanation.definitionFit: The humble-bee is the bumblebee, a social insect whose name sounds like modesty.

clue.text: Surgeon's assistant coming into line?

definitions.meaning: a hospital assistant who applies bandages to wounds
to dress ranks is to align soldiers, so one doing so comes into line

explanation.definitionFit: A dresser assists a surgeon by dressing wounds, and in drill one who dresses is one forming up in line.

clue.text: Swimmer overturned arguments noisily in course of meal

indicators.note: overturned means the word for quarrels is turned upside down, so in a down clue it reads backwards

parts.note: rows are quarrels

indicators.note: in puts the musical letter inside the word for a course

parts.note: a dish is one course of a meal
F is forte, loudly, in music

explanation.surface: Upended quarrels erupt loudly during dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' makes SWOR from ROWS, and 'in' puts F (forte, music's mark for loud) inside DISH to give DFISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A swordfish is a large ocean fish, so it swims.

clue.text: Perhaps met in church first to raise money

indicators.note: first puts the abbreviation for the church at the front of the answer

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A churchgoer meets someone at the service to start a fundraising drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' turns MET IN into NTIME, and 'first' puts CE (Church of England) ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A centime is a small coin, a hundredth of a franc.

clue.text: Going on interminably with no purpose?

definitions.meaning: lacking an end in the sense of an aim or goal

explanation.definitionFit: Endless means never stopping, and read as end-less it means having no aim.

clue.text: They root for it in Perigord!

definitions.text: They root for it in Perigord!

parts.words: They root for it in Perigord!
parts.note: root here means dig with the snout, as pigs do when hunting a prized fungus in the Dordogne, not cheer

explanation.definitionFit: Pigs are used to find black truffles, the prized underground fungus of the Perigord region of France.

clue.text: Extend the professional pine finish

indicators.note: finish tells us the word for yearning comes at the end, after the first piece

parts.note: a professional is a pro
to pine is to long

explanation.surface: A craftsman stretches out the varnish on pine furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine finish' reads like a wood stain, but 'finish' places LONG last.
explanation.definitionFit: To prolong something is to make it last longer.

clue.text: Creature grasping gold — the agent of all our woes

definitions.text: the agent of all our woes

indicators.note: grasping means the animal holds the heraldic word for gold inside it

parts.note: a panda is a creature
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An animal clutches gold, the cause of all mankind's misery.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Pandora opened the jar that released every evil into the world.

clue.text: Sounds like what foremen do abroad

indicators.note: Sounds like says the word for the foremen's job is to be heard, not read

parts.note: foremen supervise, or oversee, workers

explanation.surface: A question of what a factory supervisor does when working in another country.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversea is an adjective or adverb meaning across the sea, in a foreign land.

clue.text: Cucumber produced by woman in Gateshead family

indicators.note: in places the word for a woman inside the other two pieces combined

parts.note: read as gate's head, the first letter of gate
kin are family
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A Tyneside household's woman grows a pickling vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England; split as Gate's head it gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: A gherkin is a small cucumber used for pickling.

clue.text: Ambiguity from Butler needed no translation

indicators.note: translation turns words into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A butler's remark was so clear it required no interpreting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' rearranges BUTLER NEEDED NO; the irony is that a phrase with two meanings would need explaining.
explanation.definitionFit: A double entendre is a word or phrase with two meanings, one usually risque.

clue.text: Two pages needed for extended table?

definitions.meaning: a sheet in a book, printed on both sides, holds two pages
a hinged or extra flap that lengthens a dining table

explanation.definitionFit: A leaf of a book is one sheet with a page on each side, and a table leaf is the insert that enlarges it.

clue.text: Handel, we hear, was sometimes hagridden

definitions.text: Handel, we hear, was sometimes hagridden

parts.words: Handel, we hear, was sometimes hagridden
parts.note: the composer's name sounds like a handle, and a long wooden handle with bristles is what witches, or hags, ride

explanation.definitionFit: A broomstick is the long handle of a broom, and witches are pictured riding one.

clue.text: Old ascetic's directions about Indonesian currency

definitions.note: the possessive 's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: about means the compass letters go round the coin

parts.note: E, S and E are compass directions
the sen is a hundredth of the Indonesian rupiah

explanation.surface: An ancient hermit gives directions about money in Indonesia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the compass points E, S, E around SEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an austere Jewish sect of the time of Christ.

clue.text: Honour gained by Jean Paul in the long run

indicators.note: gained by means the abbreviation is acquired by the revolutionary, so it follows his name

parts.note: Jean-Paul Marat was a leader of the French Revolution
Hon is short for Honour or Honourable

explanation.surface: A Frenchman named Jean Paul eventually wins an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the long run' looks like 'eventually' but defines a 26-mile race.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a footrace of about 26 miles, a very long run.
